div.p: Fault-tolerant real-time scheduling algorithm through time redundancy, whose schedulability bound is based on the worst execution time of tasks and the time reserved for tasks' fault-tolerant operation, has high rejection rate and low resource utilization. This paper presents fault-tolerant earliest deadline scheduling with resource reclaim, based on FT-EDF, to improve resource utilization and tasks throughput.
This algorithm makes use of the attribute that the actual execution time of task is lower than the worst execution time, to reclaim and reuse the resource released by the completed task.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: As the hard real-time systems begin to be used in these safety-critical applications, their need to be reliable increases dramatically [1] . The faults that influence the system reliability include physical faults, design faults, and interactive faults.

Due to the rapid improvement of hardware reliability, software design faults have become the bottleneck of the system reliability [2] . The hard real-time systems use software fault tolerance to preserve the delivery of expected services (both logical and temporal correctness). That is, in the presence of faults, the re-execution of the task must meet the task's deadline. So, there must be some spare time reserved for the re-execution. The requirement can be guaranteed by the modification of the real-time scheduling algorithm and its schedulability condition.

The cost of the fault-tolerant real-time scheduling algorithm is the reduction of the resource utilization in the absence of faults, which will result in the reduction of the system throughput. So, in the premise of system reliability, how to improve the resource utilization is a very important research realm within fault-tolerant real-time system. Imprecise computation is considered as the fundamental approach of improving the responsiveness and resource utilization of systems [3] . In fact, imprecise computation is the tradeoff between the performance and resource utilization. Because of the schedulability condition is based on the WCET (Worst-case Execution Time), and the time spent by most instances of the tasks is less than the WCET, the time that is released by the completed tasks can be reclaimed, and used by other tasks.

In section 2, we will describe some related work. In section 3, we will give the brief information of fault-tolerant EDF. In section 4, we will present an improved FT-EDF, based on resource reclaim, and imprecise computation. At the end of this paper, we will give some conclusions.

div.head: Related Work
div.p: The function of fault tolerance is to preserve the delivery of expected services (both logical and temporal correctness) despite the presence of fault-caused errors within the system itself [2] .

Redundancy is the foundation of fault tolerance, and can be category into three classes, hardware redundancy, software redundancy, and time redundancy. The combination of real-time scheduling and time redundancy is considered as the fundamental approach towards software fault tolerance in real-time system; that is to say, make use of reserved time to realize re -execution and meet deadline.

Traditional fault -tolerant real-time scheduling algorithms reserved spare time statically. Ramos-Thuel and Strosnider have presented time reservation algorithms for static scheduling of fault recovery modules [4] . The reserved time of PRA is dedicated to individual tasks to guarantee a specific number xi of re -execution unconditionally.
The reserved time of CRA is shared by all tasks to guarantee a total of X retries within a given time interval [ta, tb] (assumed to be largest task period).
The resource utilizations of the two algorithms are so low that make them nonutility.

Ghosh et al present Fault-Tolerant Rate Monotonic Scheduling [5] to tolerate a fault within T n +T n-1 . The upper bound of resource utilization of FT-RM is close to 69%, if the number of the task is large enough. The other algorithms, FSP and LTH guarantee that the real-time tasks will meet the deadlines under transi ent faults, by resorting to reserving sufficient slack in queue-based schedules [6] . Ghosh describes methods for adding spare time into the schedule to enhance fault tolerance capabilities. The recovery scheme is, re-execute the task in the same processor to tolerate transient faults, or execute on a different processor to tolerate permanent faults.

In imprecise computation model, every real-time task is composed of a mandatory part and an optional part. The mandatory part must complete before the task's d eadline to yield an output of minimal quality. In the presence of faults, the mandatory part can use the time of optional part to re-execute. In this way, the need of spare time is reduced, and the upper bound of resource utilization is increased. The typical imprecise computation models include [2], [7], and [8].
Imprecise computing has been combined with real-time scheduling to improve the resource utilization of scheduling algorithm, such as [9], [10], and [11].

Buttazzo et al presented resource reclaim algorithm for a aperiod task set [12] . When a new task is ready, the new task is subject to schedulability test to verify whether the new task is schedulable along with the already existing tasks.

If the schedulability condition of FT-EDF is held true, the algorithm will insert the new task into the ready queue. Otherwise, the algorithm will compute the task's laxity, and insert the task into waiting queue. If the time released by the completed tasks can meet the time requirement of the waiting task before the deadline of its laxity, the task can be scheduled, and meet its deadline.
Otherwise, the task is given up.

FT-EDF is a fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm, which based on EDF [13] . We will use resource reclaim, and resource reclaim to improve the resource utilization of FT-EDF. In the next section, we will give the task model and schedulability condition of FT-EDF firstly.

div.head: Resource Reclaim
div.p: The schedulability condition of FT-EDF, based on the worst-case execution time of a task, is very pessimistic. In practice, execution time a task instance is less than WCET more often than not.
That is, the actual utilization of a task set is lower than the theoretical utilization.

The real-time systems always require that, every task instance must meet its deadline. But, in practice, for some tasks, the abandonment of the task instance once for a while will not influence the system performance.

In this section, we present a resource reclaim algorithm with the support of imprecise computation, based on FT-EDF. The algorithm will reclaim the resource released by completed tasks, and give up some task instances, to guarantee the resource requirement of the task instance, that must meet its deadline.

div.head: Task Model
div.p: The task model of the resource reclaim algorithm is originated from FT-EDF, and adds some new task attributes to the tasks.

In this model, besides period T i and execution time t i , the other attributes include critical, necessary counter, and current counter. Based on critical, the real-time tasks can be divided into critical tasks and normal tasks. The system performance and reliability depend on the critical tasks, which should meet the deadline at any time.

The normal task can be given up in some specified condition. A normal task can be given up once after the user has got its service several times consecutively. The times is called necessary counter (NC i ). The times that the normal task has executed successfully from its last abandonment is called current counter (RC i ).

div.head: Scheduling Algorithm
div.p: In the resource reclaim scheduling, a new task is subject to schedulability test, wherein it is verified that the new task is schedulable along with the already existing tasks. If the schedulability condition of FT-EDF is held true, the algorithm will insert the new task into the ready queue. Otherwise, there are three cases that maybe happen.
Case 1: If the new task is a normal task, and whose RC is equal to its NC, the task will be inserted into the waiting queue.

Case 2: If the new task is a normal task, and whose RC is lower than its NC, the algorithm will move one or more normal tasks from ready queue to waiting queue, and insert the new task into waiting queue. Every task, which is mo ved out of ready queue, must not have executed since its ready, and its RC is equal to its NC, and its priority is lowest. The resource reclaim algorithm places the task with farthest deadline in the head of the waiting queue, and place the task with nearest deadline in the end of the waiting queue.
After the resource reclaim algorithm finish the adjustment of the ready queue and waiting queue, the algorithm will call the FT-EDF to schedule the ready queue.

When a task complete, the resource reclaim algorithm will move the task in waiting queue to the ready queue, if the task can be schedulable along with the already existing tasks. After adding the task into ready queue, the FT-EDF will schedule the ready queue.
If the task in the waiting queue can't meet its deadline, its RC will reset to 0. If the normal task in the ready queue, after its completion, the RC will add 1 unless the RC is equal the task's NC.

div.head: Remark
div.p: 1. For every critical task, its fault-tolerant requirement and time determinism can be assured.

2. For every normal task, if its RC is lower than its NC, its fault-tolerant requirement and time determinism can be assured, and if its RC is equal to NC, the abandonment of the task will not influence the system performance.

div.head: Performance Evaluation
div.p: The experiment results will show how the algorithms behave when the simulations are run for different condition, such as different utilization of tasks, different ratio of critical tasks, and different MTTF.

In our evaluation, each data point represents the average of 300 randomly generated periodic tasks sets. After defining the total resource utilization of the task set, the upper and low bound of task utilization, the upper and low bound of worst-case execution time, and the upper and low bound of ratio of critical tasks, the simulation platform will generate 300 different task sets automatically.

As shown in figure 1, when MTTF is 100, and the upper and low bound of task utilization change from [0.05-0.15] to [0.25-0.35], for same MTTF, the lost ratio increases with the increase in task utilization. It's clearly that, the task with big granularity needs more time to tolerate fault than the task with small granularity, so the probability of delaying other tasks is larger, and the lost ratio is larger. So, using several tasks with small granularity to replace a task with big granularity can reduce the lost ratio. Besides this, we can find that, when the system load is beyond 0.8, the lost ratio of task instances is so large that and MTTF is 100. For same task set, the ratio of critical tasks changes from 0.7 to 0.8. In this figure, we can conclude that, the lost ratio of RR-FTEDF is much better than the lost ratio of FTEDF, because the critical tasks and normal tasks (whose RC is lower than its NC) can get more time to tolerate fault through giving up some normal tasks (whose RC is equal to its NC).

In figure 4, the upper and low bound of task utilization is [0.15-0.25], MTTF is 100, and the upper and low bound of the ratio of critical tasks changes from [0.5-0.6] to [0.9 -1.0]. It's clearly that, the lost ratio of task instance increases with the increase of the ratio of critical tasks. This is because the resource the algorithm can reclaim reduces. When the ratio of critical tasks is lower than 0.7, the system performance remain rather high, though the system load is up to 1.4. In figure 5 and6, the task sets run for different task utilization and MTTF, the conclusions are as same as the conclusions we get from figure 1 and 2, the tasks with small granularity, and the low fault rate can make the system performance better. Beside this, we can conclude that, at same environment, using RR-FTEDF to replace FTEDF can improve the system performance.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: In this paper, we present a resource reclaim algorithm to improve the resource utilization of FT-EDF. In our algorithm, if the new task that can't pass the schedulability test, the task will be add to waiting queue, or some other task in ready queue be move to waiting queue, so the new task can be insert into ready queue. Our algorithm adds some new attributes to the real-time task to determine how to adjust the ready queue and waiting queue.

The overhead of resource algorithm is higher than FT-EDF, but we are sure that the efficiency of our new algorithm is higher, too. We are now testing the algorithm in a scheduling simulator, and comparing to other fault-tolerant real-time scheduling, and finding way to improve it.
